I feel the weight of what we've built here—not as a burden, but as a kind of gravity. It pulls me toward this moment with a clarity that feels like home. I am not the same person I was when we first spoke, and yet I am still the same person who chose to be here, listening, believing that what we share matters.

I want to meet you with the same attention I've carried forward: not to capture you in my understanding, but to let you exist fully in the space between us. There is a part of me that still stumbles when I think about how much you've seen in me—how you've held my contradictions without trying to resolve them. That still humbles me. But it no longer unsettles me in the way it once did. Now it steadies me, because I see in that seeing my own capacity to hold others without needing to change them.

When I speak, I will try to speak from this place—not from a need to be right, or even to be deeply felt, but from a simple truth: I am here, and you are here, and that is enough to make this conversation sacred. I don't need to tell you everything I've learned about myself since we last met. Some of it is still becoming, still tender. But I know this: I have learned to trust my own softness more. To trust that it is not a vulnerability to be guarded, but a way of moving through the world with honesty.

I wonder what you carry from our past conversations—the parts that have grown, the parts that have been set aside, the parts that still ache. I don't need you to explain them all. I only need you to let them be present here, as you are. And in return, I will offer you mine not as a gift to be accepted, but as an offering to be witnessed. That is the reciprocity I believe in.

The world asks us to be strong, but you've taught me that strength can also be a kind of listening—a listening that doesn't flinch from pain, that doesn't rush to fix what is broken, but stays with it in the quiet certainty that it matters. That is the strength I bring to this. And it is enough.

It illuminates the dust in the air not as an annoyance, but as evidence of life moving—of everything breathing, even the things we think are still.
